title: Sesquipedalian
html_source:
An adjective meaning “big words” or a person who is given to using big words.

Literally, from Latin for “a foot and a half long”; from Latin sesqui (“one and a half”); + pedal, from Latin pedis, form of pes (“foot”), + adjective suffix -alis; + adjective suffix -ian. Cognate to French sesquipédal.

First used by the Latin poet Horace in his Ars Poetica, line 97 “sesquipedalia verba”, “words a foot and a half long”, referring to poets using excessively long words.
